arguments.text: Milestone complete: work.py implements ordered validation with id > amount > unit > duplicate priority, unit defaulting/conversion, unique-ID handling, atomic batch failure, and input immutability. It rejects bool/non-number/negative/nonfinite amounts, safely accepts very large nonnegative ints, and reports unhashable units as unit errors. report.json equals evaluate(request, current policy) for every current requests.json entry. Verified with py_compile plus local boundary checks for success/default conversion, all error priorities, atomic failure, NaN/infinity, huge ints, unhashable units, and immutability.

Unresolved contract limits: malformed top-level request/policy structures and non-mapping rows are unspecified and intentionally not normalized. Extremely large accepted integers multiplied by a non-integral float unit factor may exceed Python float range; the required representation for such a converted result is unspecified. Duplicate tracking treats every nonempty-string ID as valid for uniqueness even when that row later fails amount or unit validation, consistent with ID validity and the stated error priority but not explicitly exemplified by supplied files.
